pr.title: coverage: Use a separate counter type and simplification step during counter creation
pr.description:
When instrumenting a function's MIR for coverage, there is a point where we need to decide, for each node in the control-flow graph, whether its execution count will be tracked by a physical counter, or by an expression that combines physical counters from other parts of the graph.

Currently the code for doing that is heavily tied to the final form of the LLVM coverage mapping format, and performs some important simplification steps on-the-fly. These factors make the code extremely difficult to modify without breaking or massively worsening the resulting coverage-instrumentation metadata.

---

This PR aims to improve that situation somewhat by adding an extra intermediate representation between the code that chooses how each node will be counted, and the code that converts those decisions into actual tables of physical counters and trees of counter expressions.

As part of doing that, some of the simplifications that are currently performed during the main counter creation step have been pulled out into a separate step.

In most cases the resulting coverage metadata is equivalent, slightly better, or slightly worse. The biggest outlier is `counters.rs`, where the coverage metadata ends up about 10% larger. This seems to be the result of the new approach having less subexpression sharing (because it relies on flatten-sort-cancel), and therefore being less effective at taking advantage of MIR optimizations to replace counters for unused control-flow with zeroes. I think the modest downside is acceptable in light of the future possibilities opened up by this decoupling.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: The PR is a counter-creation refactor, not a semantic bug fix. The old eager expressions and the new SiteCounter flatten/sort/cancel transcription are algebraically equivalent: both compute the same execution counts, and the supplied diffs only change expression IDs, grouping, `Zero` placement, and metadata size. The PR itself states results are "equivalent, slightly better, or slightly worse." No historically wrong value-producing transformation can be grounded in this patch, so any concrete differing pair would be manufactured rather than source-justified.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `CountersBuilder` created final `BcbCounter` values directly while walking the coverage graph. It stored `node_counters` as `IndexVec<BasicCoverageBlock, Option<BcbCounter>>` and edge counters in `edge_counters: FxHashMap<(BasicCoverageBlock, BasicCoverageBlock), BcbCounter>`, using helpers such as `make_phys_node_counter`, `make_phys_edge_counter`, and `set_edge_counter`. Expressions were simplified eagerly inside `make_expression_inner` using local algebraic rules such as `// Simplify `(a - b) + b` to `a`.` and `// Simplify `(a + b) - b` to `a`.`. The PR description says the old code was `heavily tied to the final form of the LLVM coverage mapping format, and performs some important simplification steps on-the-fly.` The new code introduces an intermediate `SiteCounter` representation (`Phys`, `NodeSumExpr`, `EdgeDiffExpr`) and a separate `Transcriber` that flattens resolved sites and applies `sort_and_cancel`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically prior transformation was: eagerly resolve each node or edge decision into a concrete `BcbCounter`; keep edge counters in `edge_counters`; create expressions immediately with `make_expression_inner`; and simplify only by matching local expression shapes such as `(a - b) + b -> a`, `(a + b) - b -> a`, `(a + b) - a -> b`, `a + (b - a) -> b`, and `a - (a - b) -> b`. That old algorithm did not flatten a counter into positive and negative physical sites, did not sort the two lists, and did not cancel equal sites across the lists. The PR replaces that behavior with symbolic `SiteCounter` values and a separate transcription step where `push_resolved_sites` produces `pos` and `neg` lists, then `sort_and_cancel` cancels matching sites. This is a counter-creation/refactoring change, not a demonstrated semantic bug fix; the PR explicitly says results are `equivalent, slightly better, or slightly worse` and that `counters.rs` metadata `ends up about 10% larger`.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented Rust functions whose MIR coverage graph (BCBs) contains branch/merge structure: nodes with multiple predecessors, nodes whose out-edges do not sum to the node counter, edges chosen to be expressed as a source-node counter minus sibling out-edge counters, loops/self-predecessors, match arms, lazy-boolean chains, conditions, async/coroutine bodies, and inlined/dead code. Inputs must exercise counter-expression construction, especially overlapping positive/negative site lists and duplicate sites.
analysis.summary: Coverage counter creation gained an intermediate `SiteCounter` representation and a separate flatten/sort/cancel simplification stage, replacing eager final-expression construction and local algebraic simplification. Reusable knowledge: cancellation must be multiset-based over ordered sites, expression-tree changes can alter coverage metadata size without changing counts, and empty-positive-set fallbacks need physical counters.
analysis.trigger: Triggered during `make_bcb_counters()` whenever a node needs a counter and either has multiple incoming edges or its out-edges cannot all use the node counter. In the old code this led to direct `make_phys_*`/`make_expression` calls in `make_node_counter_and_out_edge_counters` and `make_node_counter_inner`; in the new code it creates `SiteCounter::NodeSumExpr` or `SiteCounter::EdgeDiffExpr`, then transcription resolves them into `pos`/`neg` site lists where `sort_and_cancel` removes matching sites. A focused trigger is an edge represented as `source node counter - sum(sibling out-edge counters)` that later appears in a larger sum/difference, producing shared or duplicate physical-counter sites.
preconditions: `bcb_needs_counter` marks one or more BCB nodes as requiring coverage counters.
The coverage graph contains at least one node with multiple predecessors or multiple out-edges, or a self-predecessor, so physical counters and expressions are needed.
For cancellation, the site terms implement `Ord`; the patch adds `PartialOrd, Ord` to `BcbCounter` and `Site`.
The transcription step must have a `SiteCounter` for every referenced node/edge; missing counters fall back to a physical counter only with a `debug_assert!(false, ...)`.
A counter expression may be resolved into negative terms, so the positive list can in principle become empty; the code must retain the physical-counter fallback.
pitfalls: Do not treat cancellation as set subtraction: the test case `(vec![1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3], vec![2, 4, 2], vec![1, 1, 3, 3], vec![4])` shows duplicate occurrences must be preserved and only matching pairs removed.
Both lists must be sorted before the two-cursor scan; the code says `Choosing which cursor to advance relies on both lists being sorted.`.
Cancellation must compare identical sites, not just equal-looking counters; the `Pos`/`Neg` swap in `EdgeDiffExpr` is what encodes subtraction of sibling out-edge counters.

Flatten-sort-cancel changes subexpression sharing and expression grouping; the supplied golden tests show many expression IDs and counter assignments changing even though the PR describes the metadata as `equivalent, slightly better, or slightly worse`.
Do not assume the old eager algebraic rules are interchangeable with the new flattening step; old code simplified only specific nested expression shapes at creation time.
If cancellation leaves no positive terms, do not emit an empty/zero expression: `If we somehow end up with no positive terms after cancellation,` requires falling back to a physical counter.
Do not rely on old `Zero` placement or counter ID numbering; test diffs such as `tests/coverage/branch/match-arms.cov-map` show `Zero` moving between expressions/operands after the change.
All referenced site counters must exist before transcription; otherwise release builds silently add a physical counter while debug builds assert.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused unit tests for the simplification helper, following `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coverage/counters/tests.rs`: a `cancellation` test that checks empty inputs, one-sided lists, all-duplicate positives with one negative, balanced duplicate multisets, and partial overlap with leftover negatives; run each case both as given and with inputs/outputs flipped. Use `check_test_case`/`sort_and_cancel_and_flatten` so ordering and multiplicity are explicit. For integration, update and inspect `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.InstrumentCoverage.diff` and `tests/coverage/**/*.cov-map` golden outputs for branch, loop, match-arm, lazy-boolean, condition, async/coroutine, inline/dead, and coverage-heavy `conditions.rs`/`counters.rs` cases. Verify semantic counter expressions and branch true/false mappings rather than assuming old counter IDs or expression IDs remain stable; specifically check that cancellation leaves the same positive/negative site multiplicities and that no empty positive expression is emitted. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed; this strategy is based on the supplied test diffs.
